description: Keyword (BM25) search over the body text of statute sections and, in the default source, Kansas administrative regulations, in the same snapshot as the statute tool; source=<code> searches one regulation source alone. Without jurisdiction=, results mix states: on 6,852 benchmark housing-law questions run unconfined, the top-ranked section came from a state other than the asker’s in 97.7% of them. Each row carries its jurisdiction, corpus and as_of; statute and regulation rows can appear together. Rank is textual match strength only. Keyword, not concept, with no stemming: very common words are dropped, duplicates collapse, at most 40 words run, matched any-of, so a top hit may share one word with the query; terms_searched and terms_dropped report what ran, and "double quotes" require a phrase. Only the body is searched, not the heading. Scores drift in their last digits between restarts, so close rows can swap places. Returns metadata, a snippet with [hl]...[/hl] marks and a rank; the statute tool returns the full section. A section not returned is a miss, not an absence. ends_at_colon is flagged as in the statute tool. A missing keyword index returns a visible 503, not zero matches. Every response, including 400 and 503, carries "note" and "coverage_note". The sources tool returns this tool’s full coverage statement and, per source code, its coverage and counts.

jurisdiction.description: restrict to one jurisdiction, e.g. "ks" or "us". STRONGLY preferred when the user’s state is known: without it results mix states

q.description: words to match in the statute section text. A full natural-language question is fine: common words are dropped and the rest matched ANY-OF, so more words widen the search rather than narrowing it. "double quotes" for a phrase that must appear together

source.description: omit for statutes and Kansas regulations; a regulation source code ("cfr" for federal, or a state code) searches that source alone; each code’s coverage is given by sources(tool="statute_search", source=<code>)

title.description: only with source=: narrows the search to one title, part or chapter of that source; the forms per source are given by sources(tool="statute_search", source=<code>)

name: statute_search
title: Keyword search over statute text
